paragraphs: Abbahu bar Ihi (see there) came before Shmuel, first chapter of Bava Metzia, 14a; chapter Eizehu Neshekh, 75a: Shmuel told him. At the end of chapter Haddar, 74, end of a, Ivot bar Ihi came before Shmuel, who permitted the side-post he made for an alley. Rav Anan dismantled the side-post. (Yuchasin writes that he lived with Shmuel and Rav Anan in one alley: who revealed this prophecy to him?) Binyamin (it should read Minyamin) was his brother. One would feed his servants every kind of food, and Elijah would speak with him (Ketubbot 61a). Chapter Benei Ha'ir, 28a: Abbahu and Minyamin, sons of Ihi, did not gaze at a Kuti or enter into partnership with him. Nazir, chapter 4, 24b: Shmuel said, “Do not sit on your legs until you tell me,” etc. He stated four laws.
